$comment:
REQ-RCT-002: *different regions produce clearly different hunter pools*, and exceptional recruits must be immediately legible as special.

An origin is where a candidate came from, and it is the thing that makes two recruitment pools feel unlike each other. It biases four things at once — names, archetypes, personalities and potential — because biasing only one produces pools that are nominally different and read identically. The Phase 1 TECH_DEBT entry called this out: one name pool made every region's recruits interchangeable.

`weight` is how often an origin appears at all; `reputationAtLeast` gates the rarer ones, so a guild nobody has heard of gets locals and a famous one starts attracting people who travelled to be there. That is REQ-RCT-001's "pool depends on town, reputation and region" made concrete.

Biases are *weights*, never filters. A Marsh-born Adept is unusual and entirely possible; making origins gate archetypes would turn recruitment into a lookup table and quietly destroy the variety the system exists to produce.

origins.name: Frontier-born
origins.description: Grew up within sight of the gate. Knows exactly how bad it gets out there.

origins.name: The marsh villages
origins.description: Quiet, patient people from the low country. They do not startle.

origins.name: The hill clans
origins.description: Came down for the work and stayed for the fighting.

origins.name: The collegium
origins.description: Educated somewhere with a roof and a library, and curious about what is out there.

origins.name: Off the far road
origins.description: Travelled a long way to join this guild in particular. That says something.

pool.$comment: REQ-RCT-001: the pool refreshes both on a timer and for a price. Both exist because they answer different frustrations — a player who is waiting should be able to pay, and a player who is poor should not be stuck forever.

exceptional.$comment: REQ-RCT-002's second half — an exceptional recruit must be *immediately* legible. The threshold is on the composite potential score, and the label is authored rather than derived so the writer picks the words. Nothing mechanical hangs off the label: it describes the candidate, it does not improve them.
exceptional.label: Exceptional
exceptional.note: Someone the guild would regret letting walk away.
